name: Human Revision vs AI Scientist Revision Protocol
purpose: Compare human author revision, raw AI Scientist revision, and IGRE six-gate revision under the same OpenReview peer-review signal when version-chain metadata is available.

version_chain.P0: Initial submission created before the official review-release or decision period.
version_chain.R: Human peer reviews and decision text released after P0.
version_chain.PH: Human-revised paper or camera-ready version after reviews, rebuttal, or decision.
version_chain.PAI: AI Scientist revision generated from P0 plus R under a fixed budget.
version_chain.PAI-6G: IGRE six-gate revision generated after routing R through the six gates.
version_chain.Pcontrol: No-review or shuffled/unrelated-review control generated from P0.

eligibility_rules: P0, R, and PH must be time-ordered from metadata.
Review text must be later than P0.
PH must be later than the review or decision window.
PH must never be visible to automatic generation arms.
If the dataset exposes only one paper text with no reliable version metadata, downgrade to review-signal taxonomy or mini-artifact generation.
If generation is meant to simulate the past, literature and model-access policy should be time-capped to the P0 date; otherwise label the run as retrospective replay.
claim_boundary: This is an experimental protocol. It can support future causal revision-chain comparisons only after eligible OpenReview cases are collected and generated artifacts are scored. It is not current evidence that AI or IGRE outperforms human author revision.
